Tracking and cutting costs, and practice

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; IA: Infrequent Access; EBS: Elastic Block Store; SNS: Simple Notification Service; ECS: Elastic Container Service; RDS: Relational Database Service; IAM: Identity and Access Management; VM: virtual machine

  • Explain the pricing principles and the EC2 purchasing options, and choose among them
  • Describe data transfer and storage costs
  • Explain how AWS Organizations consolidates billing and shares discounts
  • Use the Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets and the Cost and Usage Reports
  • Explain cost allocation tags and AWS Compute Optimizer

2Pricing models, data transfer, storage and estimating

Running case

Tidewater Watches Its Bill

  • Tidewater's steady servers run all year, while nightly image jobs can wait and restart
  • Photos are served to customers and copied between Regions, and the team wonders what that costs
  • The shop now has five accounts, and the finance lead wants one bill and a warning before spending passes a limit
  • Each project's cost must be visible
  • Your job: choose the pricing options and cost tools

How AWS Pricing Works [Verify live]

  • Pay as you go: you pay only for what you use, so spending follows your needs
  • Save when you commit: Savings Plans and reservations lower prices in return for a commitment of one or three years
  • Pay less by using more: tiered pricing; for example, the more you store in Amazon S3, the less you pay per GB
  • Free Tier: new accounts receive USD 100 in credits, with up to USD 100 more for activities, plus always free offers
  • As of 4 November 2026: a Free account plan lasts up to six months or until credits run out
Exam tip

Pay as you go, save by committing, and pay less per unit as volume grows.

EC2 Purchasing: On-Demand, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances [Verify live]

Option How it works Fits when
On-Demand Pay by the second, no commitment Short-term or unpredictable use
Savings Plans Commit to a USD-per-hour amount for 1 or 3 years; Compute Savings Plans also cover Fargate and Lambda and any family, size, OS or Region Steady use that may change shape
Reserved Instances A billing discount for a specific configuration for 1 or 3 years; Standard or Convertible; pay all, partial or no upfront; no cancelling Steady, known configuration
  • As of 4 November 2026: AWS recommends Savings Plans over Reserved Instances, with savings of up to 72% (up to 66% for Compute Savings Plans)
Exam tip

A commitment to a dollar amount: Savings Plans. A commitment to a configuration: Reserved Instances.

EC2 Purchasing: Spot, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances and Capacity Reservations

Option How it works Fits when
Spot Instances Spare capacity at a steep discount; EC2 can interrupt with a two-minute notice; not covered by Savings Plans Batch jobs and other interruptible work
Dedicated Hosts A physical server fully yours; shows sockets and cores; bring your own per-socket or per-core licenses; billed per host Licenses and compliance
Dedicated Instances Instances on hardware dedicated to one account; billed per instance; no visibility of the host Isolation without host control
Capacity Reservations Reserve capacity in one Availability Zone for any duration; no discount by itself Guaranteed capacity
Exam tip

Interruptible: Spot. Your own licenses: Dedicated Hosts. Guaranteed capacity: Capacity Reservations.

Choosing a Purchasing Option

  • Steady, predictable use: Savings Plans, or Reserved Instances for a fixed configuration
  • Can be interrupted: Spot Instances
  • Short-term or unpredictable: On-Demand
  • Your own licenses or strict compliance: Dedicated Hosts; Dedicated Instances for isolation only
  • Must have capacity in a zone: Capacity Reservations, combined with a discount plan
  • Mix them: commitments for the base load, Spot for extras

Exam tip

Match the need (steady, interruptible, licenses, capacity) to the option.

Data Transfer Costs

  • Into AWS from the internet: free
  • Out to the internet: charged, at rates that depend on the Region
  • Within the same Availability Zone: free
  • Between Availability Zones: typically charged
  • Between Regions: typically charged
  • Reduce it: keep traffic in a zone, use CloudFront, and use gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB, which avoid charges within a Region

Exam tip

Inbound is free; outbound and cross-Region or cross-zone traffic costs money.

Storage Pricing: Options and Tiers [Verify live]

Option What you pay for Cost trait
Amazon S3 What you store, plus requests and data transfer No overage charges; tiered by volume
S3 Standard-IA, One Zone-IA Lower storage price Retrieval fee; 30-day minimum
S3 Glacier classes Lowest storage prices Retrieval fees; minimums of 90 to 180 days
S3 Intelligent-Tiering A small monitoring fee per object No retrieval fees
Amazon EBS What you provision Pay for the size you create
  • Lifecycle rules move data to cheaper tiers automatically
  • As of 4 November 2026: minimums are from the S3 User Guide
Exam tip

Cooler data in cheaper tiers, but watch retrieval fees and minimum durations.

One Bill for Many Accounts: AWS Organizations

  • AWS Organizations manages many accounts; the management account pays the charges of all the member accounts
  • Consolidated billing gives one bill, and you can track charges per account
  • Combined usage shares volume pricing discounts, Reserved Instance discounts and Savings Plans across accounts
  • Consolidated billing has no additional fee
  • For billing, the organization is treated as one account, so a Reserved Instance bought by one account can discount matching usage in another
  • Discount sharing can be turned off in the billing preferences

Exam tip

One bill and shared discounts for many accounts: consolidated billing in AWS Organizations.

Estimating Costs: AWS Pricing Calculator

  • AWS Pricing Calculator is a free, web-based planning tool for estimating the cost of AWS services
  • Model a solution before you build it: pick services, Regions, instance types and payment options
  • It shows the calculations behind each estimate, grouped by service or architecture
  • Save an estimate as a link, or export it as CSV or PDF
  • Its prices come from the AWS Price List API, and estimates exclude taxes
  • A version inside the Billing and Cost Management console can use your discounts and commitments
Exam tip

Estimate before you build: AWS Pricing Calculator.

3Tracking and cutting costs, and practice

Tracking Costs: AWS Cost Explorer and AWS Budgets

Tool What it does Remember
AWS Cost Explorer View and analyze costs and usage with charts, filters and grouping; 13 months of history and a forecast; the console is free See where money went
AWS Budgets Set cost, usage, and Reserved Instance or Savings Plans budgets; alerts by email or SNS when actual or forecasted spend crosses a threshold Warn me before I overspend
  • Budgets data updates up to three times a day, so alerts can lag
  • Budget actions can apply a policy automatically
Exam tip

Look back and forecast: Cost Explorer. Warn on a threshold: AWS Budgets.

Organizing Costs: Cost Allocation Tags and Cost and Usage Reports

  • A cost allocation tag is a label (key and value) that organizes your costs by project, owner or application
  • Two types: AWS-generated tags (prefix aws:) and user-defined tags (prefix user:)
  • Both must be activated in the Billing and Cost Management console; tags can take up to 24 hours to appear
  • Activated tags appear in Cost Explorer and in cost allocation reports
  • AWS Cost and Usage Reports hold the most comprehensive cost and usage data, delivered to your S3 bucket as CSV files by hour, day or month, with columns for your tags
  • Only the management account manages cost allocation tags in an organization
Exam tip

Tags show cost by project, once activated; Cost and Usage Reports hold the detailed data.

Cutting Costs: Compute Optimizer and the Billing Console

  • AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes configuration and utilization metrics and gives rightsizing recommendations, and finds idle resources
  • It covers EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups, EBS volumes, Lambda functions, ECS on Fargate, RDS and more, using about 14 days of CloudWatch data by default; you must opt in
  • AWS Billing and Cost Management is the home for the Bills page, payments, credits, Cost Explorer, Budgets, tags and Free Tier tracking
  • IAM users cannot see billing until you activate IAM access; by default the root user can
Exam tip

Rightsize and find idle resources: Compute Optimizer. Bills and payments: the Billing console.

What the Exam Asks: Pricing and Cost Management

  • Commit or not: Savings Plans for a dollar amount, Reserved Instances for a configuration, On-Demand for none
  • Interruptible, licenses or capacity: Spot, Dedicated Hosts, Capacity Reservations
  • Data transfer: in is free; out to the internet, across zones and across Regions cost money
  • Storage: cooler tiers cost less to store but add retrieval fees and minimums
  • Many accounts: consolidated billing, one bill and shared discounts
  • Estimate, track, warn: Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer, Budgets
  • Organize and save: tags and Cost and Usage Reports; Compute Optimizer
Exam tip

Name the need first: commitment, interruption, licenses, capacity, estimate, track or warn.

Design Check: Tidewater's Cost Plan

Tidewater's need Choose
Servers that run all year, with room to change families Compute Savings Plans
Nightly image jobs that can restart Spot Instances
A server needing its own per-socket licenses Dedicated Hosts
Cheaper storage for records rarely read S3 Glacier class, via a lifecycle rule
One bill for five accounts, with shared discounts Consolidated billing
A cost estimate before building the new design AWS Pricing Calculator
A look back at last quarter's spend AWS Cost Explorer
An email when forecast spend passes a limit AWS Budgets
Cost per project in the reports Cost allocation tags
Find oversized servers AWS Compute Optimizer
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

Try It: A Monthly Cost Budget With an Email Alert (Optional)

  • Goal: get a warning before spending passes a limit in a practice account
  • In the Billing and Cost Management console, open Budgets and choose Create budget
  • Choose a monthly cost budget with a small amount, and add an alert at 80 percent of actual spend and another for forecasted spend, sent to your email
  • Check the Budgets pricing page: monitoring is free, but budget actions have a daily cost beyond the first two
  • Clean up: delete the budget when you finish

Lists the budgets in an account (the account ID is an example)

aws budgets describe-budgets --account-id 123456789012
Exam tip

Hands-on work is not tested on this exam, but it shows how alerts and thresholds work.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Tidewater's web servers run at a steady level all year, but the team may change instance families and Regions. Which option offers savings for a commitment while keeping that flexibility?

  • ASpot Instances, which use spare capacity that can be interrupted
  • BCompute Savings Plans, a commitment to an amount of usage per hour
  • CDedicated Hosts, which provide a physical server for your use
  • DOn-Demand Capacity Reservations, which reserve capacity in one zone only
Show the answer

Answer: B. Compute Savings Plans lower prices in exchange for a one- or three-year commitment to a usage amount, and they apply regardless of instance family, size, operating system or Region. Spot can be interrupted, Dedicated Hosts target licenses and compliance, and Capacity Reservations give capacity without a discount.

S2Tidewater's nightly image-resizing jobs can be interrupted and restarted without harm. Which EC2 option gives the lowest price for this work?

  • ADedicated Instances, which run on single-tenant hardware for one account
  • BOn-Demand Instances, which are billed by the second
  • CStandard Reserved Instances, with a three-year commitment
  • DSpot Instances, which use spare capacity at a steep discount
Show the answer

Answer: D. Spot Instances sell spare EC2 capacity at steep discounts, and work that can be interrupted and restarted suits them. Dedicated Instances add isolation at a higher price, On-Demand has no discount, and a three-year commitment is wasted on short jobs.

S3A company must use its existing per-socket server software licenses on AWS and needs visibility of the sockets and cores. Which option fits best?

  • ADedicated Hosts, a physical server that is fully dedicated to the company
  • BDedicated Instances, which run on hardware reserved for a single AWS account
  • CSpot Instances, which use spare capacity at a steep discount for interruptible work
  • DCompute Savings Plans, a one- or three-year commitment to hourly usage
Show the answer

Answer: A. Dedicated Hosts give visibility of sockets and cores and support bringing existing per-socket, per-core or per-VM licenses. Dedicated Instances give isolation without that visibility, and Spot and Savings Plans are pricing options that do not control licensing.

S4Which TWO data transfers are free of charge? (Select TWO.)

  • AData transferred into AWS from the internet
  • BData transferred out from AWS to the internet
  • CData transferred between Availability Zones in a Region
  • DData transferred between two AWS Regions
  • EData transferred within a single Availability Zone
Show the answer

Answer: A, E. Inbound data transfer from the internet and data transfer within the same Availability Zone are free. Outbound transfer to the internet, and transfer across Availability Zones or Regions, typically incur charges.

S5Tidewater wants a cost estimate for a planned architecture before it builds anything. Which tool should it use?

  • AAWS Cost Explorer, which analyzes past spending
  • BAWS Budgets, which alerts on spending thresholds
  • CAWS Pricing Calculator, a free tool for estimating costs
  • DAWS Cost and Usage Reports, which list detailed usage data
Show the answer

Answer: C. The AWS Pricing Calculator models a solution and estimates its cost before you build it. Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Reports describe spending that has already happened, and Budgets warns when spending crosses a threshold.

S6The finance lead wants an email when Tidewater's forecast monthly spend is expected to pass a set amount. Which service should Tidewater use?

  • AAWS Budgets, with an alert on forecasted cost
  • BAWS Pricing Calculator, which estimates planned costs
  • CAWS Artifact, which provides compliance reports
  • DAWS Compute Optimizer, which recommends rightsizing
Show the answer

Answer: A. AWS Budgets can alert by email or Amazon SNS when actual or forecasted cost passes a threshold. The Pricing Calculator estimates costs, Artifact provides reports, and Compute Optimizer recommends resource sizes.

S7Tidewater now has five AWS accounts in one organization. How are their charges and discounts handled?

  • AEach account is billed separately, and discounts can never be shared with the others
  • BAWS Support combines the accounts when asked, for a monthly fee for each account
  • CAWS Cost Explorer merges the invoices of all the accounts automatically each month
  • DConsolidated billing: one bill, with Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts shared
Show the answer

Answer: D. With consolidated billing in AWS Organizations, the management account pays one bill at no extra fee, and usage is combined so volume, Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts are shared. The other options describe behavior that does not exist.

S8Tidewater applied a user-defined tag named Project to its resources but cannot see it in Cost Explorer. What must it do?

  • AWait a day, because user-defined tags appear in every billing report with no setup
  • BActivate it as a cost allocation tag in the Billing and Cost Management console
  • CAttach the tag to an IAM policy so that it becomes visible in the billing reports
  • DAsk AWS Support to create the tag for the account in its internal billing system
Show the answer

Answer: B. Both AWS-generated and user-defined tags must be activated as cost allocation tags in the Billing and Cost Management console before they appear in Cost Explorer and cost allocation reports, and then they can take up to 24 hours to show.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Principles pay as you go, save when you commit, pay less by using more
EC2 options On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances, Capacity Reservations
Transfer and storage inbound is free; outbound, cross-zone and cross-Region cost money; cooler tiers cost less to store
Accounts consolidated billing gives one bill and shared discounts
Tools Pricing Calculator estimates, Cost Explorer analyzes, Budgets warns, tags and Cost and Usage Reports organize, Compute Optimizer rightsizes
